headline: Resolved the cross-family atom-namespace P1_BLOCKER at the design level: a canonical 46-atom split manifest + deterministic remap function, empirically verified against all 195 distinct placeholder ordinals in the currently-committed B0-B6 corpus (0 split-integrity violations across 1170 checks). Real tokenizer/atoms_index.json binding remains a separate, still-open gate -- correctly not claimed as solved.
state: Gabriel via coordinator: SUPERVISOR_INBOX.json flagged trigger2_canonical_tokenizer_abi_binding as P1_BLOCKER after the earlier consolidation pass found 168 distinct placeholder atom ordinals across B0-B3 (15, ordinals 0-14), B4 (60, ordinals 20-79 plus a 20-ordinal 80-99 decoy range) and B5 (93, ordinals 200-299ish) against the course document's declared 46 real accepted atoms. Scoped the problem first, as instructed: read tools/trigger2_b4_capacity_interference_generator_v1.py and tools/trigger2_b5_variable_n_equivariance_generator_v1.py directly (not assumed) and confirmed no single row in ANY family shows more than ~24 distinct atoms simultaneously (B4 worst case: capacity K<=16 + up to 8 distinct decoy fillers; B5 worst case: N<=12; B0-B3 never exceed 3) -- 46 is never a per-row capacity constraint anywhere in this repo's existing families. The 168-placeholder count is pure cross-family ID bookkeeping over many different episodes (episode-local meaning, per the course's own law), not a structural need for >46 simultaneously-existing real atoms. Sent this analysis to chatgpt-secondary for a second opinion (targeted send, confirmed successful) but before harvesting a reply, found stronger ground truth already in the repo: research_entity/global/j-space/research/2026-08-26_TRIGGER2_ABI_SYMBOL_PRIOR_CONTEXTUAL_TOKEN_AUDIT_V1_GPT56SOL.json (a prior chatgpt-secondary research delta, itself citing the ingested external XENO vector-language handoff, same abi/MANIFEST.json sha256 every family's ABI_MANIFEST_SHA256 constant already references) contains the actual 46 accepted atom NAMES (A-Z, 0-9, and 10 words: yes/no/true/false/maybe/unknown/if/then/not/and) plus the 1 rejected name ('or'), and its own H_T2_ABI_03 hypothesis explicitly calls for 'a frozen immutable atom-split manifest before real rendering' with pairwise-disjoint TRAIN/VALIDATION/HOLDOUT pools -- exactly the artifact needed here. Built tools/trigger2_canonical_atom_split_manifest_v1.py + tests (8/8 pass): splits the 46 real atom names into TRAIN_AND_VALIDATION (37: matching blueprint_v2's own train==validation-symbol-pool design) and HOLDOUT_FROZEN (9), stratified ~80/20 within BOTH the 36 neutral-alphanumeric and 10 language-bearing atom groups (source delta's H_T2_ABI_01 flags language-bearing atoms as a separate pretrained-prior risk needing independent measurement on both sides of the split) via deterministic hashlib-based ranking, not hand-picked. Provides remap_ordinal(family, ordinal, split_role, manifest) -> canonical atom name, deterministic and reproducible. Before trusting this design, empirically scanned all 14 committed B0-B6 JSONL files (not assumed from generator source alone): of 195 distinct placeholder ordinals actually in use, 132 legitimately appear in both TRAIN and VALIDATION rows (expected) and exactly 20 (B4's ATOM_POOL_DECOY range 80-99, confirmed by direct source inspection to be split-agnostic noise/filler that is never a row's actual target) appear in all three splits; after excluding that known decoy range, ZERO placeholder ordinals cross the TRAIN/VALIDATION<->HOLDOUT_FROZEN boundary anywhere in the corpus -- the split-role of every remaining placeholder is well-defined. Verified the remap function itself preserves this integrity across 1170 (family x ordinal) checks (6 families x 195 ordinals), 0 failures: every placeholder empirically used only in TRAIN/VALIDATION rows maps only into the TRAIN_AND_VALIDATION real-atom pool, every placeholder empirically used in a HOLDOUT_FROZEN row maps only into the HOLDOUT_FROZEN real-atom pool, decoys always map into TRAIN_AND_VALIDATION regardless of which split's row they appear in (proven safe: TRAIN/VALIDATION-role and HOLDOUT-role atom NAME sets are disjoint, so a decoy can never coincidentally equal a HOLDOUT row's real target). Committed research_entity/claycode/training/TRIGGER2_CANONICAL_ATOM_SPLIT_MANIFEST_V1.json and its verification report.
next: This resolves the NAMESPACE/DESIGN half of the P1 blocker (there is now a concrete, verified, deterministic path from every family's existing placeholder ordinal to one of the real 46 atoms, preserving split integrity, requiring no rewrite of any already-committed/already-audited family data). It does NOT resolve the full real-tokenizer-binding gate: exact atoms_index.json (atom-to-token-ID table), exact target tokenizer bytes/hash, and exact renderer bytes/hash all remain explicitly unresolved per the cited source delta's own 'remaining_identity_gaps' -- TRIGGER2_ABI_CONTEXTUAL_RENDER_GATE/v1 stays SPECIFIED_NOT_EXECUTED, correctly not claimed as solved here. When those artifacts become available, the actual rendering step is: for each committed row, take every ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN occurrence, determine its family + empirically-known split role (or decoy status), call remap_ordinal(), then verify the resulting real-atom occurrence against atoms_index.json for exact single-token identity before any admission credit. chatgpt-secondary's reply to the earlier atom-budget question (sent, not yet harvested -- browser daemon was mid-recovery) may still contain a useful independent cross-check once retrievable; nothing here depends on it, but it should be reviewed for disagreement in a future session per the same verify-before-accepting discipline used throughout this pass.
